title: Great American Family Selects CTS For Channel Origination, Playout, Transmission
body_html:
What Was Announced

Great American Family has selected CTS for its channel origination, playout, and transmission needs, marking a significant shift in the broadcaster's technical operations. This decision involves outsourcing critical components of its broadcast workflow to a third-party provider, which can have far-reaching implications for the broadcaster's technical infrastructure and operational efficiency. By partnering with CTS, Great American Family aims to streamline its broadcast operations, potentially reducing costs and improving reliability in the process.

The Engineering and Operational Significance

The decision to outsource channel origination, playout, and transmission to CTS is likely driven by the need to simplify operations, reduce technical complexity, and improve scalability. By leveraging CTS's expertise and infrastructure, Great American Family can potentially reduce the number of manual handoffs, improve metadata flow, and accelerate publishing, ultimately leading to more predictable output under deadline pressure. From a technical standpoint, this partnership may involve the integration of CTS's systems with Great American Family's existing media asset management (MAM) and production asset management (PAM) systems, as well as its over-the-top (OTT) and linear broadcast platforms. The use of standardized protocols such as SMPTE ST 2110 and AES67 may also be relevant in this context, enabling seamless communication between different systems and ensuring high-quality audio and video transmission.

Industry Context

The partnership between Great American Family and CTS reflects a broader trend in the broadcast industry, where media companies are increasingly seeking to outsource non-core functions to specialized providers. This approach allows broadcasters to focus on their core competencies, such as content creation and programming, while leveraging the expertise and economies of scale of third-party providers to manage complex technical operations. Comparable approaches can be seen in the adoption of cloud-based services for video processing, content delivery networks (CDNs) for OTT distribution, and automated playout systems for linear broadcasting. The use of IP-based technologies, such as those based on the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, is also becoming more prevalent, enabling greater flexibility and scalability in broadcast operations. As the industry continues to evolve, we can expect to see more partnerships and collaborations between media companies and technology providers, driving innovation and efficiency in broadcast workflows.

Implications for Broadcast and Media Teams

For engineering leads and operations managers, the partnership between Great American Family and CTS serves as a reminder of the importance of carefully evaluating technical partnerships and their potential impact on broadcast workflows. When considering similar partnerships, teams should focus on key factors such as validation, rollback, observability, and staff readiness to ensure a smooth transition and minimize disruption to existing operations. It is also essential to review the architecture and dependencies of the proposed solution, mapping out potential integration points and identifying areas where customization or additional support may be required. By taking a measured and informed approach to technical partnerships, broadcast and media teams can harness the benefits of outsourcing and cloud-based services while maintaining control over their core operations and ensuring the highest levels of quality and reliability. Ultimately, the success of such partnerships will depend on the ability of media companies to balance the benefits of outsourcing with the need to maintain editorial control, operational flexibility, and technical resilience.
